summary.title: GLUE & DesignOps
summary.description: As part of the ongoing evolution and improvement of the design system at Liverpool, we decided to integrate task automation tools, adopt new technologies such as variables in Figma, and optimize the processes of auditing and managing the system.
summary.sector: Design Ops, design system, internal services, e-commerce
summary.team: Front and back developers, UX/UI designers and researchers

context.heading: Context
context.intro: Since the creation of the User Experience and Interface department within the Digital Product Management, various efforts have been made to develop and formalize a design system. These efforts have become recurrent and have undergone multiple changes due to technological advancements and the dynamic growth of the team. In this context of evolution and continuous improvement, the history of GLUE (Global Liverpool User Experience) can be divided into four major stages.

stage1.title: Foundation and first steps
stage1.description: The project was born as a library distributed to teams via Sketch and documented in Zeplin, designed by UX consultants in collaboration with Marketing.

stage2.title: Atomic design and UI Kits
stage2.description: Atomic Design was adopted for component creation, facilitating the integration of UI Kits and the standardization of design documents. As part of this evolution, the library migrated to Figma.

stage3.title: Documentation & communication
stage3.description: A detailed documentation of the components begins, while an internal UX team takes over the maintenance of the system and the achievements of GLUE are disseminated.

stage4.title: Design Ops and engineering
stage4.description: A token system is implemented, improving communication with development and automating design processes to optimize tasks and efficiency.

context.participationIntro: My participation in GLUE focuses on four key areas:

bullets.title: 1. Adoption of technologies.
bullets.description: I seek to develop and integrate technological tools into the work environment, with the aim of optimizing workflows, providing innovative design resources for UXers, and modernizing management and design processes.

bullets.title: 2. Improvement of inputs.
bullets.description: Through audits and the definition of quality standards in design processes, I work to strengthen the governance of the design system, facilitating its use.

bullets.title: 3. Automation of processes.
bullets.description: I analyze and detect processes that can be automated in order to improve overall performance and operational efficiency.

tech.title: Technologies Used
tech.intro: As part of the updates in Figma, the integration of Variables was introduced, which represented a change in how components and tokens are generated within the design system. This process was carried out in two phases: the beta phase and the first release of the feature.

tokenizedColors.title: Tokenized colors
tokenizedColors.desc: (Normalized to the MD3 standard, replacing 3 UI Kits with 3 organized variable modes)

brandsAdded.title: Brands added
brandsAdded.desc: (13 new modes were added, thus avoiding the creation of 8 UI Kits)

tokenizedColors.title: Tokenized colours
tokenizedColors.desc: (275 new colours were added by adding modifiers to auxiliary colours)

textDecorations.title: Text decorations
textDecorations.desc: (As a basis for applying modes and variables to text in Figma)

textSizes.title: Text sizes
textSizes.desc: (Based on rem and normalized for high readability)

insumos.intro: Within the HandOff processes of the projects, different pains were improved that teams such as Development and Business Analyst had, which led to a series of works to address these problems:

fonts.subtitle: · Consolidation and care of fonts
fonts.intro: A repository was created to consolidate all the fonts used throughout the e-commerce, internal tools, and other sites belonging to Liverpool. This repository was generated in Drive and built according to the specific needs of the UX team and Front-End developers. A nomenclature was created to serve both teams and was ultimately documented within the Figma variable library.

structure.subtitle: · Structure of documents in Figma
structure.intro: As a result of a series of approaches, discussions, and surveys with teams that consult Figma documents as part of their workflow, including Frontend devs, Business Analysts, Business, and QA, a structure was generated within the Figma documents that worked to correctly accommodate and prioritize those pages that needed it. Thus, a structure was created that includes the following points.
points: Addition of emojis to improve page identification
Grouping of pages by similar semantics
Creation of three different types of documents: UX projects, research, and internal tools

summary.title: HUBBUB and the visualization of noise in Mexico City
summary.description: Website for the deployment of data on the phenomenon of noise in Mexico City and its Metropolitan Area
role: Product designer, BA, developer, project manager

context.title: Context
context.intro: The Acoustic Design Laboratory of the Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana has been researching and studying noise phenomena in Mexico City and its Metropolitan Area for over 6 years, leading to a series of needs and developments that were implemented throughout the project. By the time I joined the team, the following elements were already in place:

maps.desc: Including one general map of the city and other routes

context.participationIntro: My participation in the team was to fulfill a specific need: the design of a dissemination space for the data and concepts of the phenomenon, as well as dashboards with different views and intentions for the application report data. The entire solution design process was carried out by me and was completed in 3 phases:

research.title: 1. Research
research.description: Analysis of the problem, generation and understanding of concepts, and user and project research.

design.title: 2. Design
design.description: Definition of proposal and graphic identity, sketching of ideas and prototyping of the project.

invest.title: Research
invest.intro: Within the research stage, different efforts were made not only related to the interface and experience part, but also theoretical frameworks and a deep understanding of the concepts that would be poured into the project were required. Even a solution definition stage took place within this, being, in a very synthesized way, a stage composed of three parts.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.text: Recognition of the problem, objectives of the Acoustic Design team with their HUBBUB project, and delimitation of the theoretical framework to be presented within the topic.

research.title: Research
research.text: Research on user needs, communication spaces, benchmarks, and product design guidelines.

concepts.title: Concepts
concepts.text: Research on the phenomenon of noise and data visualization, as well as user-centered design encompassing concepts, theorems, and philosophy.

analysisSection.heading: Analysis section
analysisSection.intro: Two exercises were carried out in parallel to obtain and make a first approach to hypotheses. The first of these were interviews with the Acoustic Design Laboratory, which already had a series of data that supported the construction of a series of primary needs for the project, which are reflected in three pillars that would end up guiding the subsequent stages of research.

noise.title: About noise
noise.text: Noise is a highly studied phenomenon but rarely disseminated within Mexican culture, which has led to a lack of understanding of concepts that would help bring people closer and guide them to understand it.

harmlessData.title: Harmless data
harmlessData.text: Harmless data is data that does not cause harm or negatively affect people or the environment. In the context of noise, it is essential to identify and use harmless data to ensure responsible and sustainable design.

nonProfessionals.title: Reaching non-professionals
nonProfessionals.text: In addition to what was mentioned about harmless data, it is not only necessary to find public access spaces for this information, but it is also important to establish an appropriate level of language so that any interested party can make these concepts and information their own.

researchSection.heading: Research section
researchSection.intro: Once the problems, objectives, and scope of the project were identified, a design solution was then delineated, under a User Centered Design approach, so a series of surveys and approaches to stakeholders were conducted. The results obtained can be seen in the following graphs.

interestImportant.title: Are you interested in and do you think it is important to understand the phenomenon of noise?
data: It is important and interesting to me
It is important but not interesting to me

heardAbout.title: Have you heard about the phenomenon of noise?
data: No, I have never heard it

learnMethod.title: How do you like to learn about new topics?

wantToKnow.title: What would you like to learn about?

invest.conclusionsIntro: From all these surveys, the following conclusions could be drawn:
conclusions: The community really finds it important and interesting to talk about a phenomenon like noise.
Almost half of the respondents know nothing about the phenomenon.
Videos are the preferred medium for learning about new topics, followed by articles and websites.
The top three media through which people like to get informed are videos, articles, and websites; that is, digital media are generally preferred.
There is a greater interest in the consequences of noise, followed by its causes, and then statistics or informative data about it.
invest.solutionParagraph: This already helps to determine a website as a solution design that pours in the information from the articles published by the laboratory: two spaces within the website, one focused on context, theoretical frameworks, and even consequences, and the second as an organized consultation dashboard for the reports obtained through the application.

conceptsSection.heading: Concepts section
conceptsSection.intro: As part of the understanding and appropriation of concepts, an entire investigation was carried out, which is covered in chapters 1, 2, and 3 of the thesis SEE THE NOISE, “An exercise in information visualization for the noise of Mexico City”

design.title: Design
design.intro: Within the design stage, all efforts related to solution design were grouped, which involves different processes of graphic design, user experience, benchmarking, and interface. All these processes can be poured into three spaces.

understanding.title: Understanding HUBBUB
understanding.text: Recognition and complete understanding of the project's current graphic identity, including the formation of a graphic identity for the site.

sketching.title: Sketching
sketching.text: Externalization of ideas, paper prototyping, and exploration of different graphic visualizers.

mockup.title: Mockup
mockup.text: Refinement of ideas, creation of the experience, and lowering the interface to a high-fidelity prototype.

understandingSection.heading: Understanding HUBBUB section
understandingSection.intro1: By the time the project began, HUBBUB already had a series of channels where it displayed a certain aesthetic.
understandingSection.intro2: From all this, the color palette, iconographic style, typography, voice, and tone stood out. Certain terms and assets such as icons and logos were also rescued. All these graphic resources were poured into a new UI created for the website channel that we would develop, in addition to improving iconography, signage, and other aspects of the interface.

sketchingSection.heading: Sketching section
sketchingSection.intro: For the sketching, a series of paper sketches were made that not only allowed for quick exploration of interaction and composition ideas but also involved non-designer teams (such as laboratory members) in the idea construction process. These sketches also allowed for rapid iteration between components and identification of the types of data we wanted to display.

mockupSection.heading: Mockup section
mockupSection.intro1: Once the idea exploration phase, fueled by team feedback, was completed, we moved on to the fine mockup phase. In this phase, components and all necessary screens for both parts of the experience were created. All this work was done in Figma and, similarly, subjected to various presentations with stakeholders to make specific adjustments, such as in browsers and viewers.
mockupSection.intro2: In addition to the experience mockup done in Figma, a document of user stories and technical stories was also created to facilitate rapid implementation during the development phase. These stories were documented in the following document.

progra.title: Programming
progra.intro: The programming stage encompasses the entire process of coding and effort planning.

planning.title: Planning

progra.implementationNote: * This last stage has not been carried out as it is still awaiting approval on the business side.

summary.title: Electrolineras system, MoviLidad
summary.description: Application for the offering of charging centers for electric cars
summary.team: Front and Back developers, automotive business, business analyst, project manager

context.title: Context
context.intro: Due to the collaboration between BYD and Liverpool, along with the growing market for electric cars in Mexico, there was a need to install and offer charging points in strategic locations. Liverpool's real estate division creates a series of spaces within shopping centers like Galerías and others where Liverpool has a presence, allowing for the installation of electric charging stations within Mexico City.

stations.desc: (Distributed in the northern area of CDMX)

chargers.desc: (Located in specialized charging stations and shopping centers)

context.collabLabel: Direct collaboration with QiOn for infrastructure and Openpay for payments
context.topicsIntro: The project development topics within the UX approach that were most interesting would be these three:

research.title: 1. Research and definition of interface
research.description: Benchmarks and direct user research to define the main user flow.

notifications.title: 2. Notification environment
notifications.description: Integration of real-time activities and status for the user beyond the application and Liverpool environment.

transactionFlow.title: 3. Transaction flow and payment methods
transactionFlow.description: Modification and constant adaptation of the transactional flow, as well as the exploration of payment methods that directly influenced the user's flow.

invest.title: Research and definition of interface
invest.intro1: One of the most important parts of the application's design was the interface and how the user would have to learn to use it, as those who would use this charging network section would be users who were already familiar with it or, failing that, would have to familiarize themselves with the Pocket environment, Liverpool's application.
invest.intro2: Not only did it involve using previously used components and graphic language within Pocket, but it also had to approach what other applications in the same field already offered to the customer. With this in mind, the first steps were to generate benchmarks from multiple companies.
invest.mapIntro: Once important points such as the map as the main screen, result filtering, and prepaid transactional flows were established, it was decided to mock up an experience that approached this structure and, at the same time, included all the offers and actionables that the app itself offered. This resulted in a map like the following:
invest.testIntro: As a final part of the research and as a result of some comments from the business side, it was also decided to test the home page of the application. This was done through a survey in Maze, and the results were as follows:

first.task: The user is asked to order the options above according to their importance
first.objective: To know the user's priorities and expectations regarding the application's capabilities
first.result: In order of relevance, the options were arranged: Map, Navigation, Wallet, History, and Help
conclusions: The Map becomes fundamental for the user as it describes a natural flow for locating charging stations, which will subsequently enable the rest of the transaction flow, which is ultimately the main task to be performed.
Navigation, which involves the user's ability to use the map and the rest of the application's activities, appears as complementary to exploration and, consequently, remains relevant.
The Wallet becomes the third fundamental option of the application by enabling the user to make payments and, consequently, complete the last part of the main journey.

second.task: The user is asked to choose which of the two options seems more appropriate to access the different options offered by the application, in addition to complementing their choice with an open question to express their reasons.
second.objective: To guide the interface towards an option that functionally and aesthetically meets the needs of our user, in addition to gathering qualitative information about their choice.
second.result: The most chosen screen was number one, with a preference of 69% of respondents.
conclusions: The majority of users expressed a preference for screen number 1, accompanied by comments highlighting a clean interface and simpler navigation, even considering the position of the options pill.

ambNoti.title: Notification environment
ambNoti.intro1: Another effort made for this project, which involved the implementation of a technology that had never been used within Pocket, was real-time activities. For the first time, there was a need to display information with real-time tracking that could add value to the customer experience, along with the technical capabilities provided by QiOn's CMS.
ambNoti.intro2: Three specific spaces were identified where using these activities would be very beneficial:

charging.title: 1. Charging in progress
charging.description: Information such as total charging time, kilowatts charged, and current battery percentage of the car is displayed. The main animated component shows the progress of the charging.

completed.title: 2. Charging completed
completed.description: Displays instructions for disconnecting the car and uses a timer to show the time remaining before charging the parking fee begins.

fee.title: 3. Parking fee charge
fee.description: The same disconnection instructions as before are shown, along with the parking fee cost. The animated component changes to a stopwatch.

ambNoti.outro: The entire integration of the notification environment not only involved the creation of these notification modes but also prompted the research and documentation of design standards from Material Design by Android and the Human Interface by Apple. This was reflected in the documentation of Liverpool's design system with the addition of materials, effects, and animations.

flow.title: Transactional Flow and Payment Methods
flow.intro: Among all the flows that make up the charging network application, the main and most important one is the transactional flow, which allows for the vehicle's charge to be processed and the service fee to be generated.

text: This is the main page of the application, from which all secondary actions to manipulate the information displayed on the map are derived, and at the same time, it allows access to other sections of the application.

On this screen, you can see the city map with the charging stations. Its purpose is to allow identifying where the charging stations are located, information about them, and to start the transactional flow by scanning the QR code attached to the charging totem.
The device's camera is activated and the code printed on the charging totem is read.
At that moment, the information of that charging gun is loaded and the charging configuration is proceeded.

The charging gun information is loaded, which includes: identifier, station name, charger type, charging speed, charging fee, and idling fee. In addition to this information, it allows configuration through 3 types of inputs which can be by the amount of money to recharge, final percentage to leave the vehicle, or the amount of kilowatts to be charged.

Once the charge is configured, the transactional flow is initiated. The rest of the information is for selecting the payment method, giving the option to select one of the methods already saved in their Liverpool wallet or registering a new one, plus the addition of using the balance they have in their digital wallet.
Much of this configuration depends on how the e-commerce checkout was already behaving.
This page briefly shows the progress of the car's charge as well as information for any problems that may arise, from charger information to a button for interrupting the charge.
It is accompanied by a real-time activity that reflects the same experience.

Once the charge is completed or interrupted, it moves to the status of completed charging where the user is asked to disconnect their car and leave the charging area, otherwise, idling charges will begin.
This message is also accompanied by a real-time activity that warns the user of the amount of time left before idling charges begin.
Here the application starts to add a fee per minute for the car's stay in the charging area. It is accompanied by a real-time activity that adds up the minutes spent and their equivalent in fees.
Once the entire charging process is completed and no issues have arisen, a summary of the charge for all the activity performed is displayed, and the charge is processed automatically.

flow.testFlowsIntro: This flow underwent different modifications based on the payment methods and the type of payment gateway that could be implemented within the flow, which led to a series of iterations. A summary of the types of flows proposed is as follows:

autoCharge.title: Flow with automatic charge
autoCharge.text: In this proposal, licenses can be stored during the charging process, allowing for the charge to be made to the selected card at the beginning and displaying the thank you page at the end.

doubleAuth.title: Flow with double authentication
steps: Card selection, license entry, and pre-charge
doubleAuth.text: In this proposal, the aim is to make a charge based exclusively on the configured charging amount. At the end, the customer is asked to re-identify themselves to adjust the balance, either by charging or refunding.

refund.title: Flow with refund
steps: Card selection, license entry, and pre-charge of excess amount
refund.text: In this proposal, the aim is to charge an excess amount of money to ensure the collection of all types of concepts, and subsequently generate the refund.

future.title: Future steps
future.intro: The next steps for the product are primarily focused on three specific improvements with business objectives.

wallet.description: Implementation of recharges and sale of physical balances in the form of credits for use within the application. It would be understood as a new payment method.

realtime.description: Integration of other notification technologies such as StandBy, WearOS notifications, and other spaces

loyalty.description: Includes couponing, rewards program, gamification, and special deals.

intro.title: This is me
intro.subtitle: I leave you this section so you can learn more about me — beyond my work, there are other things about me that may be interesting.

music.title: Listening to and playing music is wonderful
music.p1: I love listening to music, and not just as background noise while walking around the city — I really enjoy taking my time to sit down and listen to a good album by Pink Floyd, Gorillaz, or Joji.
music.p2: I also play and sing; I really enjoy taking my guitar, my melodica, or the electric guitar, turning on the amplifier, and playing for hours and hours.
music.recentlyListening: Recently, I have been listening to:

sport.title: I love swimming
sport.p1: I have been swimming for more than a year now and I couldn't be more in love with this sport — it's an incredible feeling to get lost in the water after a day of work.
sport.p2: If I had to make a tier list of which stroke I like the most...

games.title: I prefer singleplayer games...
games.p1: I like games where I find myself alone, discovering a great story. I'd say my favorite genres are walking simulators, metroidvanias, and classic platformers. My favorite game is definitely Hollow Knight.
games.boardParagraph: Lately I've been collecting and discovering board games I've loved. I don't have many in my collection yet, but soon I'll be surrounded by them.

food.title: Asian food, cooking, and a recipe
food.p1: I love eating, but I also love cooking. Some of the things I cook most often are Asian dishes, from savory ones like ramen, gyozas, or onigiri to sweet ones like matcha ice cream. I obviously love Mexican food too — I make a spectacular birria, and I'll leave you a recipe for raw green salsa so you can enjoy it with your family.
recipeSteps: Chop the celery stalk, tomatoes, mint leaves, and serrano pepper.
Juice the lemon and the orange; set aside.
Grind everything in a mortar or blender and add salt and oregano to taste.
If needed, add water little by little — in the blender or the mortar — until you reach the consistency you like best; I prefer it a bit thicker.
Serve with tortilla chips, or use it for tacos.

manga.title: Slices of life, terror, and mechas?
manga.p1: I'm more of a manga reader than an anime watcher, and that's led me to some incredible authors who've given me both great and rough moments. Here's my manga top picks, though if you can, you should read more about the author too.
manga.animeIntro: Even though I prefer the manga format, there are some works I honestly couldn't enjoy any other way than in full color and animated. I'd really recommend checking them out — you might like them a lot.
